title: Veterans Pension Service, Age and Claim Date Figures
content:
# Veterans Pension — service, age and claim-date figures

The figures below apply without variation to every rate category: Basic Rate, Housebound and Aid and Attendance, each with no dependents or with one dependent.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Minimum active duty for a veteran who entered service before September 8, 1980, with at least one day during a wartime period | 90 days |
| Minimum continuous active duty for an enlisted veteran who entered after September 7, 1980 (or the full period called up) | 24 months |
| Age at which a veteran is treated as permanently and totally disabled for pension purposes | 65 years |
| Days after VA receives an intent to file during which a completed pension claim takes that date | 365 calendar days |
| Days before the date of claim to which an original award can reach back when a disability prevented filing | 365 calendar days |
| A veteran entitled to both Veterans Pension and Disability Compensation is paid the greater benefit absent a written election | Yes |

## Points of application

- Service: 89 days of active duty does not reach the 90-day figure; 90 days does. For an enlisted veteran entering after September 7, 1980, 24 months of continuous active duty, or the full period for which he was called up, satisfies the figure.
- Age: a veteran on his 65th birthday is at the age figure; a veteran aged 64 is not, and qualifies on age grounds only by one of the other routes the entitlement rule names.
- Intent to file: a completed claim received 365 days after the intent to file falls within the figure; one received 366 days after does not.
